answers.label: Benefits and challenges of consequential methods
answers.text:
The GHGP Project Standard must be aligned with the Corporate Standard to make consequential accounting useful for companies.

Consequential carbon accounting based on the proposed approach will phase inconsistency issues towards established attributional carbon accounting procedures following the GHG Protocol Corporate Standard. Whereas within the latter, GHG reductions are calculated by comparing annual emissions against an actual base year value, the proposed consequential modelling approach calculates GHG reductions by comparing annual emissions against fictional baseline values. For consistency reasons, the GHG Project Protocol should be aligned with the Corporate Standard regarding the baseline reference being an actual fixed base year value.

It is currently unclear whether the proposed consequential methods should be applied within corporate accounting or project-related accounting. This should be made clearer, including the goal of the AMI TWG.

answers.label: Context on test feasibility
answers.text:
The proposed additionality test must be described in more detail in order to be able for stakeholders to provide a final feedback.

The information provided regarding each additionality test is not sufficient to provide a final feedback on the matter. Though, basing on the currently available information, it seems like no project would be able to attain “additionality” after performing the tests. If reaching “additionality” is very difficult or impossible, it will neither be attractive for companies to perform several time-consuming tests nor trying to achieve “additionality”.

Another proposal with more detailed descriptions of each test should be made available by the authors to facilitate another feedback survey on the topic.
